prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a passenger and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1454; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Driver 1 was traveling southbound on a Pearland, Texas roadway when the vehicle drifted into the northbound lane and struck the front of Driver 2's vehicle in a low-speed head-on collision. Passenger was seated in the front passenger position of Driver 1's vehicle and was confirmed present by both officers on scene and by statements from independent witnesses. Several witnesses stated that the collision occurred as described by both drivers, and Driver 2 gave a consistent account of the sequence of events. Photographs taken at the scene show front-end damage to both vehicles that corresponds with the direction and force of impact reported. No prior damage to either vehicle was observed or reported by the drivers. Passenger reported neck and back pain shortly after the collision and was evaluated at the scene, where the complaint was considered consistent with the mechanism of a crash of this type. Driver 1 identified the registered owner as a member of the same household, and the owner's records were reviewed on scene. No citations were issued at the time of the report, and the investigation remains open pending further statements.
